subject: Tyska
title: Comparisons and daily life
sourceSummary: Comparative and superlative adjectives, and reflexive verbs for daily routines.

questions.opener: Most adjectives form the comparative with -er.
questions.explanation: The regular comparative is formed with -er: "schnell" → "schneller" (faster).
The superlative is formed with "am" + adjective + "-sten": "am schönsten" (nicest/most beautiful).

questions.prompt: Which word is irregular in the comparative ("better")?
questions.opener: Just like Swedish "bra – bättre" (good – better) is irregular.
questions.explanation: "Gut" (good) has the irregular comparative form "besser" (better). The superlative is "am besten" (best).

questions.prompt: What does "Ich stehe um sieben Uhr auf" mean?
questions.opener: "Aufstehen" is a participle-like verb where "auf" ends up at the end of the sentence.
choices: I go to bed at seven o'clock
I get up at seven o'clock
I eat breakfast at seven o'clock
I come home at seven o'clock
questions.explanation: "Aufstehen" means "to get up/rise". In the present tense the verb splits: "ich stehe ... auf" (I get up).

questions.prompt: What does "Ich dusche mich jeden Morgen" mean?
questions.opener: A reflexive verb for daily routines.
choices: I go to bed every evening
I brush my teeth every morning
questions.explanation: "Sich duschen" means "to shower", and "ich dusche mich" is "I shower (myself)": "I shower every morning".

questions.prompt: Write the German verb for "to go to bed" in its basic form (infinitive) — a reflexive verb.
Correct the error: "Mein Haus ist kleiner als deins, aber mein Garten ist guter."
questions.opener: "Gut" has its own irregular comparative form.
questions.answer: Mein Haus ist kleiner als deins, aber mein Garten ist besser.
steps: "Guter" is wrong — "gut" is conjugated irregularly in the comparative.
Full sentence: "Mein Haus ist kleiner als deins, aber mein Garten ist besser." (My house is smaller than yours, but my garden is better.)

questions.prompt: How do you form comparisons and describe a daily routine in German?
questions.opener: Comparative/superlative and reflexive verbs for everyday life.
questions.answer: Comparisons: adjective + -er = comparative (schnell → schneller) · am + adjective + -(e)sten = superlative (am schnellsten) · ... als = ... than · gut → besser → am besten (irregular) · groß → größer → am größten (irregular). Daily routine (reflexive verbs): sich aufwecken/aufstehen = to wake up/get up · sich duschen = to shower · sich anziehen = to get dressed · frühstücken = to eat breakfast · sich hinlegen = to go to bed. Reflexive pronouns: mich, dich, sich, uns, euch, sich.
